facts.value: Accepts the Council of Ephesus formula that one is the nature of the incarnate Word, and does not accept the Council of Chalcedon.

citations.excerpt: On the question of Christology, it accepts the definition set by the Council of Ephesus, that "one is the nature of the incarnate word". It does not accept the Council of Chalcedon (451), and renounces the teachings of Nestorius and Eutyches.

facts.value_before_verify: Accepts the first three ecumenical councils and Ephesus's formula of one nature of the incarnate Word, but not Chalcedon. Liturgy in classical Armenian.

citations.excerpt: But later on, about 480, and throughout the following centuries, the Armenians rejected the decrees of Chalcedon and held that the assertion of two natures in Christ was a relapse into the heresy of Nestor.

facts.value: The autocephalous national church of Armenia, whose historical centre is Etchmiadzin near Yerevan.

citations.excerpt: The historical centre of this autocephalous national church is the Mother See of Etchmiadzin, near the capital city of Yerevan.

facts.value_before_verify: The national church of Armenia, centered at Etchmiadzin near Yerevan, with patriarchates in Jerusalem and Constantinople.
